organizations.csv: No key column was declared. c01 looks like the account key but it is only 98.2% unique over 1017 parsed values (999 distinct), so roughly 18 rows share an id, and 13 rows have no id at all. organization_id must be unique and re-sending an id with different content is a 409 conflict, so duplicates and blanks have to be resolved by the engineer at validation before load.

organization.lifecycle_status is required but c03 is blank in 44 rows (4.3%), and organization.billing_country is required but c06 is blank in 59 rows (5.7%). Both need a decided default or an exclusion rule at validation.

Rule 2 (accounts with no activity in the last 18 months are dormant and must be loaded as Inactive) cannot be applied from this file: organizations.csv contains no activity or last-touch data. It must be applied from the activity export, after this load, or the statuses from c03 will overstate how many accounts are active.

Rules 4 and 7-12 concern subscriptions (Strategic -> Enterprise, Legacy Gold, quarterly billing, paused/expired statuses, dead trials, CAD amounts). None of them can be exercised here because organizations.csv has no plan, billing cycle, seats, status or MRR column. The subscription/billing export is needed; in particular rule 4 will need a reconciliation pass against the 85 Strategic accounts in c09.

Dates in c08 and c14 arrive in six different formats and only ~15% are ISO; both columns also contain a handful of future values (4 and 5 respectively, up to 2027-09-03). If c08 is confirmed as customer_since, future start dates are almost certainly data errors and should be surfaced at validation rather than silently loaded.

c12 is fully populated but has 30 addresses that are duplicates after normalization and 39 malformed values. Since the primary contacts derived under rule 1 must be unique per organization (and email is unique within an organization), the engineer should check whether the normalized duplicates are shared mailboxes across different accounts (allowed) or genuine conflicts within one account.

Assumption made throughout: this file produces one organization record plus one primary contact record (from c12 and c13, is_primary = true per rule 1) per row, and no subscription or activity records.
contacts.csv: 22 rows (1.0%) have no value in c01, the presumed account reference. contact.organization_id is required and must point at an existing organization, so those contacts cannot be loaded as-is; the engineer should decide at validation whether to hold them back or match them by email domain.

c18 shows 106 malformed email values and 66 normalized duplicates. contact.email is required and must be unique within an organization, so after lowercasing some accounts will have colliding addresses; resolve at validation (dedupe or suffix) rather than at mapping.

If c21 really is the primary flag, 942 rows are true across only 1046 distinct account numbers, so some accounts will carry more than one primary and others none. Meridian rejects more than one is_primary = true per organization, so a tie-break is needed - rule 1 says the account row's primary_contact_email is authoritative and can be used both to pick the winner and to fill accounts with no flagged primary.
c22 mixes six date formats with only 16.6% ISO and contains 8 future dates; whichever destination is chosen it needs a multi-format parser and a decision on the future-dated rows.
No target exists for a contact-level opt-out preference (c23); flagged for the customer rather than silently dropped because rule 14 treats opt-out as a preference that survives migration.

c17 is a single full-name column feeding two required target fields (contact.first_name and contact.last_name); only first_name could be named in the mapping row, but the stated transformation populates both.
subscriptions.json: Rule 11 (trials older than 90 days are not migrated) requires a cut-off date: the engineer should filter rows where c27 normalizes to trial and the parsed c29 start date is more than 90 days before the agreed migration/go-live date. 84 rows carry status 'trialing' and 27 carry plan 'Trial'; these sets may not be identical and should be reconciled before the filter runs.

Rule 7 depends on the seat count, but c28 is null in 41 rows (4.1%). Any 'Legacy Gold' row with a missing seat count cannot be classified as enterprise or professional deterministically; the engineer should list those rows for the customer rather than defaulting silently.

Rule 4 (Strategic accounts always carry an Enterprise subscription, billing is wrong when it disagrees) is a cross-dataset override: it can only be applied after the organization rows with customer_tier = Strategic are loaded. Expect some rows in c25 to be overridden to enterprise after the join.

c31 has a minimum of 0 and a maximum of 40000 with 75 CAD rows migrated unconverted (rule 12); the resulting mrr_usd totals will be mixed-currency by design and should be handed to finance for true-up after go-live.

Date quality: only ~18% of c29/c30 values are ISO and six formats are present, including %m/%d/%y, which is ambiguous for two-digit years. c29 has 2 future values and c30 has 80; renewal dates in the future are expected, a future start date is not and should be reviewed at validation.

c01 is assumed to be the legacy account number linking to organization.organization_id (903 distinct values over 1003 rows). If the organization dataset keys on a different column, this mapping must be revisited, since no subscription can load without a resolvable organization_id.
activity.csv: Row counts line up as follows: 2563 rows carry a currency code 'USD' in c32, and c36 has 1913 parsed values plus 650 placeholder tokens = 2563. That strongly suggests amount and currency are populated exactly on the monetary rows (Invoice 1245 + INVOICE 244 + Payment 1074 = 2563), and that the 650 placeholders are monetary rows whose amount was lost or masked. Flag those 650 rows to the customer at validation; whether they load as null amount is an engineer decision at that stage.

c34 contains a case variant ('Invoice' 1245 vs 'INVOICE' 244) and an apparent duplicate vocabulary ('Ticket' 618 vs 'Support Ticket' 394). Both are folded by the enum mapping above, but confirm with the customer that these are not two distinct legacy concepts.

c35 ranges to 2026-09-11, i.e. dates in the future relative to a present-day migration. Future-dated activities may be scheduled items rather than things that occurred; the engineer should decide at validation whether to load them into activity.occurred_at.

Customer rule 2 (accounts with no recorded activity in the last 18 months are dormant and must be migrated as organization.lifecycle_status = 'inactive') is evaluated from this dataset. The latest c35 per organization_id should be computed and fed back into the organization load; note that only 1000 distinct organization ids appear here, so accounts absent from activity.csv have no activity at all and fall under rule 2 as well.

Every c01 value must exist as an organization.organization_id before these activities load (cross-record rule: an organization must exist before any activity references it). Reconcile the 1000 distinct ids against the accounts dataset before the run.
No clarification is raised about blanks in c37 (24.5% null) or the placeholder amounts; both targets are nullable and the handling of blanks is a validation-stage decision.

rows.reason: Integer business key, 98.2% unique, 5-digit values in a 10000-98343 range on the organization row; the catalog says the customer's legacy account number usually lands in organization.organization_id, and the other entities' organization_id values must reference it.
Free text, 96.7% unique, max length 34, shapes like 'Aaaaa-Aaaaa' and 'Aaaaaa AAA' are typical company names; organization.name is the only required string name field on the entity.

Nine distinct account-state values (Active, Inactive, Prospect, Churned, On Hold, Closed) that line up with the required enum prospect/active/inactive/churned, and the customer's rule 6 explains the two values that are not in the enum.

Short sector codes (MFG, CONST, LOG, TECH, HC, ENR, PS, OTH) map one-to-one onto the organization.industry enum; the two numeric values 31 and 23 look like NAICS sector prefixes and need confirmation before they are translated.

55 distinct values that are a mix of two-letter codes ('AB', 'GA') and full state/province names ('Colorado'); organization.billing_region is described as a state or province code and is the only regional field.

Nine distinct country spellings (US, USA, United States, U.S., Canada, CA, CAN, MX, Mexico) and organization.billing_country is the required ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 field; rule 5 warns that 'CA' is ambiguous between Canada and California.
URL-shaped values (scheme://www.domain.tld) on the organization row; organization.website is the only URL field in the catalog.

One of two date columns; c08 holds the earlier minimum (2016-11-06 vs 2016-12-31 for c14), which fits a relationship start date, but nothing in the column name confirms it and the organization entity has only one date field, so which of c08/c14 is 'customer since' is the customer's call.

Silver/Gold/Bronze/Strategic/Platinum is the customer_tier of rule 3; organization.account_priority (standard/priority/strategic) is the only enum it can land in, since the catalog states priority is not the same thing as the plan and no subscription row exists in this dataset. How the spend bands collapse onto standard vs priority is a business decision.

Currency-formatted amounts from 100,000 to 45,000,000 with a mean around 23M on the organization row; that magnitude is company revenue, matching organization.annual_revenue_usd, not subscription MRR.

Integer counts from 22 to 3999 with a mean of 1938 on the organization row; that is headcount-sized and organization.employee_count is the natural home, but subscription.seats is a possible alternative reading and no other subscription columns exist in this file to settle it.

A fully populated email column on the account row; rule 1 says the account-level primary_contact_email is authoritative and should be used to create or flag the primary contact, so it belongs on the contact entity, not the organization (which has no email field).

Person-name shapes ('Aaaaa Aaaaaa'), fully populated, sitting next to the primary-contact email; it supplies the required contact.first_name and contact.last_name for the primary contact created under rule 1. The catalog has no single full-name field, so the value feeds two targets and only first_name can be named here.

A second date column with the same six mixed formats and a range (2016-12-31 to 2027-09-03) that extends into the future; the organization entity has only one date field, which c08 is proposed for, and the renewal/start date fields live on subscription, which cannot be created from this file. Its destination depends on what the column means.

Four recurring free-text operational notes ('acquired by parent co', 'renewal call scheduled', 'moved HQ 2024', 'do not contact billing before 9am') on the account row; they could be kept as organization.tags labels or as activity records of kind 'note', and which one the customer wants is a business decision.
100% unique, no nulls, single shape 'CT-000102' - a per-contact surrogate key, and it already satisfies the contact_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$.

Integer key with 1046 distinct values across 2279 rows (roughly two contacts per value) in the 10000-79936 range; this is the legacy account number the contacts hang off, which the catalog says lands in organization.organization_id and is referenced by contact.organization_id.

Shapes 'Aaaaa Aaaaaa' with 96.5% uniqueness and max length 27 indicate a single full-name column; the target splits names into contact.first_name and contact.last_name, so this one source field feeds both and only the first can be named here.
Typed as email with local@domain shape and no nulls; contact.email is the only email field in the catalog and is required.
Phone-typed column with North American shapes ((999) 999-9999, 999-999-9999, 999.999.9999); contact.phone is the only phone target and it requires E.164.

Twelve free-text role labels (Billing, Primary, Technical, Ops Manager, Purchasing, CTO, billing contact, Owner, IT, Main, CEO, AP) match contact.role, but customer rule 13 collides with the target enum (it sends CEO/CTO to primary/technical while the enum has a separate 'executive' value) and does not cover Ops Manager, Purchasing or Main.

Boolean column whose true share (942 of 2104 populated rows, ~45%) is close to one per account across the 1046 distinct account numbers in c01, which fits is_primary; the other boolean c23 (only 214 Y) fits the marketing opt-out of rule 14. The column names are anonymized, so the assignment of c21 vs c23 is inferred from distribution only.

A date spanning 2016-2027 on a contact row has no target: the contact entity has no date fields, and organization.customer_since is an account-level date that this per-contact column would overwrite inconsistently (2279 contacts over 1046 accounts). Needs a human decision before it can be dropped or redirected.

Clean Y/N flag with only 214 Y (9.4%); by elimination against c21 this is the marketing opt-out referenced by rule 14. Meridian's contact entity has no opt-out or preference field and organization.tags is account-level, so there is no home for it.

Identifier with shape AAA-99999 and examples SUB-00415 / SUB-00699, 100% unique with no nulls or duplicates; it is the natural stable key for the subscription record and already satisfies the id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$.

5-digit integer in the 10000-89979 band with 903 distinct values over 1003 rows (several subscriptions per account), which matches the catalog note that 'the customer's legacy account number usually lands here'; it is the only field on this row that can carry the required link to an organization.

Categorical plan names (Enterprise, Pro, Professional, Starter, Legacy Gold, ENT, ...) that the customer's rules 7 and 8 explicitly translate into the subscription.plan enum; only the value 'Trial' (27 rows) is not covered by any rule.
Six values (M, A, monthly, annual, yearly, Q) that are plainly billing frequencies, and rule 9 tells us exactly what to do with the quarterly code; target enum is monthly/annual.

Subscription lifecycle values (active, trialing, past due, canceled, paused, expired) that line up with the subscription.status enum, with rule 10 covering the two values that have no direct equivalent.

Small set of round integers (5, 10, 15, 25, 40, 60, 100, 250) typical of seat tiers, and rule 7 refers to a seat count on the subscription to split Legacy Gold between enterprise and professional; subscription.seats is the only integer field in the target entity.
One of two date columns; c29 starts earlier (2016-12-09) and has only 2 future values, whereas c30 has 80 future values, which is the signature of start_date versus renewal_date.

Second date column, later range (2017-02-24 to 2027-09-14) and 80 future values, consistent with a forward-looking renewal date; the target requires renewal_date to be after start_date, which fits this pairing.

Money column with mixed representations ('USD 60', '5100', '$40,000.00') on the subscription row; rule 12 states the billing export amounts are already monthly regardless of billing frequency, so it maps directly to monthly recurring revenue.

Currency code (USD 928, CAD 75) with no currency field anywhere in the target catalog; rule 12 makes it redundant because CAD amounts are loaded into mrr_usd as-is with no conversion, so the column carries no information the target can store.
Fully populated, 100% unique identifier with shape AAA-9999999 and an 'ACT-' prefix on an activity dataset; values already satisfy the activity_id pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$.

Integer in a tight 10000-10999 band with only 1000 distinct values across 4947 rows: a repeating foreign key to the legacy account number, which the catalog says lands in organization.organization_id; activity.organization_id is the required reference on this entity.

Eight categorical values (Invoice, Payment, Login, Ticket, Note, Support Ticket, INVOICE, Call) that line up with the required activity.kind enum invoice/payment/support_ticket/login/note; only 'Call' has no obvious enum member.
The only datetime column, fully populated and near-unique per row; activity.occurred_at is the required timestamp of the activity.

Numeric money-like column (25 to 10000, mean ~5027) present on roughly the same number of rows as the USD currency column, which matches the optional, nullable activity.amount_usd; it is mixed text ('1475.0' and '5725') so it is not yet a clean decimal.

Single-valued currency code ('USD' on all 2563 non-blank rows) and the activity entity has no currency field - the money field is activity.amount_usd, already USD-denominated. Customer rule 12 also says amounts migrate as USD regardless, so the column carries no information that changes the load.

Short free-text-style labels ('escalated: parts delay', 'renewal discussion', 'monthly invoice', ...) that read as the human-readable summary of the activity; activity.description is the only optional, nullable string on the entity.
